Interior Shutters

Interior shutters are a timeless choice that adds elegance and functionality to any room. Available in various materials and finishes, they can seamlessly integrate with your existing decor or become a striking focal point. Options include classic wood or durable composite, providing diverse aesthetic and practical advantages.

Exterior Shutters

Exterior shutters provide a classic architectural element that enhances curb appeal while offering practical benefits such as protection from the elements and improved insulation. They are a popular choice for homes in coastal areas like Stuart, Florida, where they can withstand salt spray and strong winds. For a comprehensive overview of exterior shutter options and their benefits, explore our guide to Hunter Douglas Shutters.

Exterior shutters offer more than just curb appeal; they provide a layer of protection and can significantly enhance your home's energy efficiency. These robust installations are designed to withstand the Florida climate, adding both beauty and resilience. They are an excellent investment for homeowners looking for durability and style.

  • Plantation Shutters: Known for wide louvers, offering excellent light control and a classic aesthetic.
  • Café Shutters: Cover only the bottom half of the window, providing privacy while allowing natural light from above.
  • Shaker Style Shutters: Feature a minimalist design with clean lines, perfect for contemporary or transitional homes.
  • Panel Shutters: Solid panels that can be closed for maximum privacy and light blockage.
  • Louvered Shutters: Traditional style with adjustable slats, offering versatility in light and airflow.
  • Board and Batten Shutters: A rustic, farmhouse-inspired design, often used for exterior decoration.
  • Bahama Shutters: Top-hinged exterior shutters that prop open from the bottom, popular in coastal regions for shade and privacy.
